hypothesis: The 'Metabolism' subtype is a well-differentiated, HNF-driven OXIDATIVE-METABOLIC state
evidence_summary: Lineage TFs, OXPHOS/FAO pathways, glutathione detox, and OXPHOS complexes all co-vary (mean r=0.66) and all split EMT/Metab; recovered by 4 analyses and consistent with the authors' G-Int/intestinal mapping.
key_limitation: Convergence is across methods on ONE dataset, not independent validation; lineage vs metabolism causally unresolved.
validation: HNF4A/HNF1A knockdown or over-expression -> measure OXPHOS proteome + oxygen consumption (Seahorse); HNF4A ChIP for FAO/OXPHOS targets; test in an independent GC proteomic/transcriptomic cohort.

hypothesis: Metabolism subtype depends on RTK->RAS-ERK signalling (MEK node); EMT subtype on PI3K-AKT-mTOR/SGK
integrates: 3.H1 + 3.H2 (cross-validated by the paper's own drug data)
evidence_summary: Motif-based kinase activity (phosX) independently reproduces the paper's MEK (Metabolism) vs mTOR (EMT) sensitivities and adds the upstream RTK layer (Metabolism) and the SGK arm (EMT, explaining pan-AKT failure).
key_limitation: PTM data are from the paper supplement, not quantms; kinase inference is motif-based; the paper's drug data are not independent of the same cell lines.
validation: pERK vs pAKT/pNDRG1 immunoblot by subtype; MEK vs mTOR vs SGK inhibitor sensitivity; multi-RTK vs single-RTK inhibition (test RTK redundancy).

hypothesis: The Metabolism subtype carries a glutathione/antioxidant programme -> ferroptosis (GPX4/GCLC) vulnerability
evidence_summary: GCLC/GCLM/GPX4/GSTs/G6PD coordinately higher in Metabolism (p=0.001), co-regulated with OXPHOS; STRING confirms a glutathione/ROS network (FDR 1e-22). A specific, actionable, previously un-nominated vulnerability.
key_limitation: Single analysis; abundance not flux; the vulnerability itself is a prediction, untested.
validation: GPX4 inhibitor (RSL3/ML210) + erastin + BSO sensitivity in Metabolism vs EMT lines; DepMap GPX4/GCLC/SLC7A11 dependency; lipid-ROS measurement.

hypothesis: A MYC-target / proteostasis (UPR) proliferation axis varies ORTHOGONALLY to the metabolic subtype
evidence_summary: MYC-target abundance tracks the UPR machinery (r=0.87) and DNA repair; this axis is statistically independent of the metabolic subtype axis (r=-0.24), so it is a second source of heterogeneity.
key_limitation: MYC/UPR gene-set member overlap inflates r; single-dataset; proliferation state also co-varies with culture conditions.
validation: After removing set overlap, re-test MYC-UPR coupling; proteasome/HSP90/IRE1 inhibitor sensitivity in MYC-high lines (NCC24, KatoIII, eAGS, AGS).

hypothesis: In-vitro EBV infection imposes a cell-intrinsic immune-evasion state (MHC-I / IFN down)
evidence_summary: The cleanest contrast in the project (isogenic, replicate-level): EBV infection lowers MHC-I antigen presentation and the interferon response. Mechanistically coherent with herpesvirus immune evasion.
key_limitation: One infected line; eAGS is also more proliferative; not linked to the main subtype axis.
validation: Flow cytometry for surface HLA-I +/- IFN-gamma in AGS vs eAGS and other freshly infected lines; CD8 T-cell killing; test EBV latent-gene (BNLF2a) dependence.
